headline: FED SPLITS 9-8: WARSH GOES SILENT ON DOT PLOT FOR FIRST TIME IN 13 YEARS — GOLD DROPS $37, SEPTEMBER HIKE ODDS SURGE TO 67%
snippet: The Federal Reserve's June meeting minutes, released July 8, showed 9 of 18 participants expect at least one rate hike before year-end versus 8 projecting no change — and Chair Kevin Warsh became the first Fed chair to withhold a dot-plot projection since the system launched in 2012, a silence the market read as deliberate ambiguity rather than consensus. Gold dropped $37 to $4,068 immediately on the release while September rate-hike probability rose to 67%; the next reset comes July 14 with the June CPI print, which now carries outsized weight as the decisive swing factor for precious metals and mining equities through year-end.

headline: OSISKO CARIBOO: ALL 11 HOLES HIT ≥1.8 G/T AU BELOW 700M — 13.19 G/T OVER 3.60M IN VIRGIN BC GROUND (TSXV:ODV)
snippet: Osisko Development (TSXV: ODV) released assays from 11 surface diamond drill holes at its Cariboo Gold Project in British Columbia — all 11 returned composites above 1.8 g/t Au and 10 returned mineralisation outside the current Mineral Resource, extending the deposit well below its current average depth of approximately 350 metres. Best intercepts include 13.19 g/t Au over 3.60 metres at 596 metres vertical depth and 28.90 g/t Au over 0.50 metres at 718 metres vertical depth, with five surface rigs continuing to push toward an 800-metre test ceiling as part of a fully funded 70,000-metre campaign targeting a significant expansion of Cariboo's known gold inventory.

headline: ARRAS DOUBLES DRILL TO 40,000M AFTER $25M RAISE — 4 RIGS ACTIVE AT BEREZSKI NORTH PORPHYRY IN KAZAKHSTAN (TSXV:ARK)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Arras Minerals Corp.
snippet: Arras Minerals (TSXV: ARK) confirmed July 9 that it is doubling its 2026 Kazakhstan drill program to 40,000 metres after closing an upsized C$25 million bought deal, with four rigs active on the Berezski North and Berezski Central copper-gold porphyry discoveries at its 100%-owned Elemes Project in northeastern Kazakhstan. To date 27 holes and over 18,000 metres are completed — with assays pending from the majority of holes due to lab volume delays — giving the company continuous momentum through two full exploration seasons on a porphyry belt that remained virtually untested until Arras moved in; the financing underwrites operations to end of 2027.

headline: ALKANE BJÖRKDAL: GOLD TO 762M DEPTH, 86.1 G/T OVER 1.25M — DEEPEST HIGH-GRADE IN SWEDISH MINE'S HISTORY (ASX:ALK)
snippet: Alkane Resources (ASX: ALK) reported July 9 that 29-hole, 15,568-metre infill and extension drilling at the producing Björkdal gold mine in central Sweden — Scandinavia's largest operating gold mine — has extended high-grade gold to 762 metres below surface via hole MU25-030, which returned 86.1 g/t Au over 1.25 metres (0.80m estimated true width) from the Eastern Extension. With the Northern Extension slated to receive a dedicated underground drill platform in FY27, Alkane is running a two-front near-mine expansion program on a mine already operating above nameplate throughput, a combination of production momentum and organic reserve growth that de-risks future production at current gold prices.

headline: TROILUS Z87: 164M AT 0.95 G/T AUEQ IN UNSAMPLED HISTORIC HOLES — MORE GOLD INSIDE THE PIT THAN MODELLED (TSX:TLG)
snippet: Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG) released results from seven additional holes at the Z87 Reserve Pit at its Chibougamau, Quebec project — with drillhole 87-26-507 returning 164 metres at 0.95 g/t AuEq, a materially larger mineralized zone than the 98-metre historic hole it was re-testing, and a second hole finding 39.6 metres at 0.82 g/t AuEq in a block of the resource model currently modelled as containing no significant gold. With 20 holes and 5,563 metres completed of a ~24,000-metre Z87 pit optimisation programme, the systematic finding that unsampled historic intervals hold more gold than expected will directly improve the strip ratio in Phase 1 pit planning — a material cost-reduction benefit before a single tonne is mined.

headline: COPPER FALLS TO $6/LB TWO-WEEK LOW — CHILE MAY OUTPUT OFF 13% YOY, IRAN DOLLAR-SURGE KILLS DEMAND OUTLOOK
snippet: Copper futures extended their decline to $6.02 per pound on July 8 — a two-week low — as U.S.-Iran military escalation amplified dollar strength and dampened the global manufacturing outlook, compounding data showing Chilean copper production fell 13% year-on-year in May. The confluence of hawkish Fed minutes, a stronger dollar, and geopolitical-driven risk aversion creates a short-term bear case for base metals that currently overrides the structural supply tightness thesis; Chile's underperformance is bullish for copper's multi-year outlook but cannot compete in the short run with real-yield and dollar headwinds that are pricing copper as though macro demand has already slowed.

headline: RELEVANT GOLD SECURES 110-PAD BLM PERMIT IN WYOMING — 5,000M FUNDED DRILL PROGRAM LAUNCHES AT BRADLEY PEAK (TSXV:RGC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Relevant Gold Corp.
snippet: Relevant Gold Corp. (TSXV: RGC) announced July 9 that the U.S. Bureau of Land Management approved an expanded five-year Plan of Operations at its Bradley Peak Gold Camp in central Wyoming — authorizing up to 16 acres of surface disturbance, 110 drill-pad locations, and concurrent reclamation — immediately followed by launch of a fully funded 5,000-to-7,000-metre drill program targeting multiple plunge corridors and the BPEX shear zone identified in 2025 drilling. The multi-pad BLM authorization gives Relevant significant operational flexibility across the broader claim block, an unusual regulatory position for a junior at this stage; Wyoming's state support for critical minerals exploration, including prior geophysical grants, reinforces the jurisdiction's cooperative permitting posture.

headline: U.S. GOLDMINING DRILLS FIRST WHISTLER HOLE — $2B NPV, 25+ PORPHYRY TARGETS IN 53,700-ACRE ALASKA BLOCK (NASDAQ:USGO)
snippet: U.S. GoldMining (NASDAQ: USGO) commenced its 2026 programme at the 100%-owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project in Alaska with the first rig deployed ahead of schedule, targeting a minimum of 6,000 metres across 8 to 10 of more than 25 systematically delineated porphyry targets within a 7.5-by-4.5 kilometre cluster on 53,700 acres of State of Alaska mining claims, approximately 105 miles northwest of Anchorage. The project's 2025 PEA models an after-tax NPV5% of $2.0 billion and a 33% IRR at specified metal prices using only the Whistler deposit's indicated resources, meaning the adjacent Raintree and Whistler East targets — yet to be drilled — represent incremental resource upside; initial assay results are expected by end of Q3.

headline: SWOT: PRECIOUS METALS SURGE ON WEAK JUNE JOBS DATA — PALLADIUM LEADS, FOMC MINUTES THEN REVERSE THE MOVE
snippet: U.S. Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT analysis documents how precious metals staged a broad rally after June payrolls missed expectations — palladium gaining 2.25%, gold jumping 2.5%, and silver surging 3.85% as September rate-hike probability fell — before the July 8 FOMC minutes partially reversed the move by confirming a 9-8 split on rate hikes. The analysis also highlights a less-discussed supply bottleneck in copper: Middle East conflict has disrupted sulphuric acid supply chains in the Gulf region, a chemical critical to heap-leach copper processing that most commodity price models have not yet incorporated as a sustained supply constraint.

headline: ABCOURT FLORDIN: 153M AT 0.5 G/T AU, 10.9 G/T HIGH-GRADE HIT — ABITIBI SOUTH ZONE CONFIRMED TO 200M DEPTH (TSXV:ABI)
snippet: Abcourt Mines (TSXV: ABI) released July 8 the first South Zone assay from its 2026 Flordin programme in Quebec — returning 153 metres at 0.5 g/t Au including a 2.1-metre interval of 10.9 g/t Au, confirming continuity of the South Zone structure to at least 200 metres vertical depth. The result contributes to a 20,000-metre programme targeting the Cartwright and 25-02 structures at Flordin, adjacent to the company's Sleeping Giant mine where underground economics require demonstrated grade continuity above the deposit's typical narrow high-grade corridor model; confirming broader envelope grades matters as much as the high-grade hit for bulk mining scenario planning.
